therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: gastric adenosquamous carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with glandular and squamous differentiation.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric tubular adenocarcinoma
description: A variant of gastric adenocarcinoma characterized by prominent dilated or slit-like tubules.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: granulosa cell tumor
description: A slow-growing, malignant tumor, characterize by the presence of granulosa-like cells and Call-Exner bodies, that is almost always found in the ovary. In rare cases, it has also been found in the testicle. There are two types of granulosa cell tumor that can be distinguished under the microscope: the adult and the juvenile. The testicular juvenile granulosa cell tumors are perhaps the most common congenital testicular neoplasms.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: hydrolethalus syndrome
description: Hydrolethalus (HLS) is a severe fetal malformation syndrome characterized by craniofacial dysmorphic features, central nervous system, cardiac, respiratory tract and limb abnormalities.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: indeterminate colitis
description: It describes patients in whom a diagnosis of ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease cannot be made based on standard clinical testing, including colonoscopy, imaging, laboratory tests, and biopsy.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|gastrointestinal disease

name: infectious colitis
description: A viral or bacterial infectious process affecting the large intestine.
therapeutic_areas: infectious disease|gastrointestinal disease|immune system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: lactic acidosis
description: Metabolic acidosis characterized by the accumulation of lactate in the body. It is caused by tissue hypoxia.
therapeutic_areas: nutritional or metabolic disease|phenotype

name: lung carcinoid tumor
description: A neuroendocrine neoplasm that arises from the lung. It is characterized by the presence of uniform polygonal cells with small or moderate amount of cytoplasm and inconspicuous nucleoli. The cells are usually arranged in organoid and trabecular patterns. It is classified as typical or atypical carcinoid tumor based on the number of mitotic figures and the absence or presence of necrosis. Atypical carcinoid tumors have a worse prognosis.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: meningeal tuberculosis
description: A bacterial infection of the membranes covering the brain and the spinal cord caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
therapeutic_areas: infectious disease|nervous system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|phenotype

name: metaplastic breast carcinoma
description: A group of invasive breast carcinomas characterized by the presence of an adenocarcinomatous component which is admixed with a dominant component that is composed of squamous cells, spindle cells, or mesenchymal cells.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: nephrosclerosis
description: Hardening of the kidney due to infiltration by fibrous connective tissue (fibrosis), usually caused by renovascular diseases or chronic hypertension. Nephrosclerosis leads to renal ischemia.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cardiovascular disorder

name: ovarian clear cell adenocarcinoma
description: A malignant glandular epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of clear and hobnail cells. It is highly associated with ovarian endometriosis, pelvic endometriosis and paraendocrine hypercalcemia.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma
description: A malignant serous cystic epithelial neoplasm arising from the ovary. It is characterized by the presence of glandular, papillary, or solid structures. Psammoma bodies may be present. In well differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells resemble the cells of fallopian tube epithelium. In poorly differentiated cases the malignant epithelial cells show anaplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: pancreatic adenocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the pancreas
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|phenotype

name: papillary lung adenocarcinoma
description: A morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of papillary structures.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype

name: pleomorphic breast carcinoma
description: A rare, aggressive, high grade invasive ductal carcinoma, not otherwise specified. It is characterized by the presence of pleomorphic and bizarre malignant cells that constitute more than 50 percent of the malignant cellular infiltrate.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: pulmonary tuberculosis
description: A bacterial infection that affects the lungs and is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Most patients with tuberculosis do not have symptoms (latent tuberculosis) and are not contagious. When signs and symptoms occur (active tuberculosis), patients become contagious. The signs and symptoms include chronic cough with blood-tinged sputum, night sweats, fever, fatigue, and weight loss.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|infectious disease

name: renal leiomyoma
description: A leiomyoma that involves the kidney.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: reproductive system neoplasm
description: A benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm affecting the male and female reproductive system.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: sex cord-stromal tumor
description: A neoplasm involving a sex cord.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: squamous cell breast carcinoma
description: A rare carcinoma that arises from the breast parenchyma and is entirely composed of squamous cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: Wilms tumor
description: An embryonal neoplasm characterized by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components. The vast majority of cases arise from the kidney. A small number of cases with morphologic features resembling Wilms tumor of the kidney have been reported arising from the ovary and the cervix.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: nasal cavity squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the nasal cavity mucosa. Signs and symptoms include nasal fullness and obstruction, pain, epistaxis, and the presence of a nasal mass.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: nasopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the nasopharynx.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: cervical artery dissection
description: A tear within the wall of any of the arteries of the neck (carotid artery or vertebral artery) and that allows blood to separate the wall layers. By separating a portion of the wall of the artery (a layer of the Tunica intima or tunica media), a dissection creates two lumens or passages within the vessel, the native or true lumen, and the "false lumen" created by the new space within the wall of the artery.
therapeutic_areas: cardiovascular disorder

name: lactose intolerance adult type
description: Adult onset lactose intolerance
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|phenotype|nutritional or metabolic disease|genetic, familial or congenital disease|gastrointestinal disease

name: acinar prostate adenocarcinoma, foamy gland variant
description: A variant of acinar prostate adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of malignant cells with abundant xanthomatous appearing cytoplasm.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: acinar prostate mucinous adenocarcinoma
description: A usually aggressive morphologic variant of acinar adenocarcinoma of the prostate gland characterized by the presence of lakes of extracellular mucin. This diagnosis applies when at least 25% of the resected tumor contains extracellular mucin.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: ACTH-producing pituitary gland adenoma
description: An adenoma of the pituitary gland that produces corticotropin. The vast majority of cases are associated with Cushing disease. Clinical manifestations include truncal obesity with thin extremities, thinning of the skin, osteoporosis, and a tendency to bruise easily. Silent or hormonally non-functioning ACTH producing adenomas have also been described. They produce symptoms of a mass-related lesion.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: ACTH-producing pituitary gland carcinoma
description: A rare, hormonally functioning or non-functioning pituitary gland adenocarcinoma that produces corticotropin. It may be associated with Cushing disease.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: adenofibroma
description: A benign neoplasm characterized by the presence of connective tissue stroma and epithelial structures. It occurs in the ovary, fallopian tube, uterine corpus, and cervix. Cases of adenofibroma of the ovary with low grade malignant potential have also been reported.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
description: A benign, slow growing neoplasm arising from tooth-forming tissues. The vast majority of cases are intraosseous and most often grow in the maxilla. It is characterized by the presence of odontogenic epithelium which is embedded in a connective tissue stroma. Local excision is curative and recurrences are very rare.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: adenosquamous carcinoma
description: A carcinoma composed of malignant glandular cells and malignant squamous cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: adrenal gland myelolipoma
description: A benign soft tissue lesion arising from the adrenal gland. It is composed of mature adipose and hematopoietic/lymphoid tissues.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: adrenal gland neuroblastoma
description: A neuroblastoma arising from the adrenal gland.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: adrenal medullary hyperplasia
description: A hyperplasia that involves the adrenal medulla.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder

name: AIDS-related primary central nervous system lymphoma
description: A lymphoma (non-Hodgkin or Hodgkin) arising from the central nervous system and occurring in HIV-positive patients.
therapeutic_areas: infectious disease|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: ameloblastic carcinoma
description: A rare, cytologically malignant ameloblastoma that may metastasize.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: anal melanoma
description: A melanoma arising from the anus. Clinical presentation includes rectal bleeding, tenesmus, pain, and change in bowel habit. The prognosis is usually poor.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: anal squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from the anal canal or the anal margin (perianal skin). Human papillomavirus is detected in the majority of cases. Homosexual HIV-positive men have an increased risk of developing anal squamous cell carcinoma in comparison to the general male population. Symptoms include anal pruritus, discomfort when sitting, pain, change in bowel habit, and bleeding. The prognosis is generally better for anal margin SCC than for anal canal SCC.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: angiolipoma
description: A lipoma with prominent vascularity. The vascular tissue is more abundant at the periphery of the tumor and contains fibrin thrombi. It occurs more frequently in younger individuals as a painful subcutaneous nodule, often on the arms.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: angiomyxoma
description: A benign soft tissue neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic spindle and stellate cells, and vascular proliferation in a myxoid stroma.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: appendix adenocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the vermiform appendix.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: appendix adenoma
description: A circumscribed neoplasm arising from the glandular epithelium of the appendix. Morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. According to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. The dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: appendix hyperplastic polyp
description: A non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the appendix. It is characterized by the presence of elongated serrated crypts and the absence of atypia or dysplasia.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: appendix neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade tumor with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the appendix. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder

name: appendix villous adenoma
description: An adenoma arising from the appendix. It is characterized by the presence of villous epithelial structures and it is associated with dysplasia.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: ascending colon neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the ascending colon. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: Askin tumor
description: A primitive neuroectodermal tumor (small round blue cell tumor) of the thorax which can involve the periosteum, thoracic wall and/or pleura though it spares the lung parenchyma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: atypical carcinoid tumor
description: A carcinoid tumor characterized by a high mitotic rate, often associated with the presence of necrosis and nuclear pleomorphism.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: atypical endometrial hyperplasia
description: An endometrial hyperplasia characterized by cytologic and architectural changes which may lead to endometrial carcinoma. Despite the atypical features and possible course, there is debate on whether to consider this a neoplasm. The relationship with endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia is also unclear.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: atypical lipomatous tumor
description: An intermediate, locally aggressive lipomatous neoplasm. Microscopically, the adipose tissue contains large and pleomorphic lipoblasts, and is dissected by fibrous septa containing spindle cells. It requires a wide local excision, may recur locally, but never metastasizes.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: atypical lobular breast hyperplasia
description: Lobular neoplasia characterized by lobular epithelial proliferation that does not completely fill the lobular unit of the breast.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: basaloid carcinoma
description: A malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, small amount of cytoplasm, and peripheral nuclear palisading.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: benign adrenal gland pheochromocytoma
description: A sporadic or familial pheochromocytoma that is confined to the adrenal gland and does not have any metastatic potential. The majority of cases are sporadic, and usually unilateral. Familial cases are usually bilateral.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: benign carotid body paraganglioma
description: A carotid body paraganglioma that is confined to the site of origin, without metastatic potential.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: benign conjunctival neoplasm
description: Abnormal growth of the cells of the conjunctiva without malignant characteristics.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: benign smooth muscle neoplasm
description: A benign mesenchymal neoplasm arising from smooth muscle tissue.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: benign thyroid gland neoplasm
description: A benign neoplasm arising from the thyroid gland.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: bile duct adenoma
description: A benign, well-demarcated polypoid neoplasm arising from the bile duct epithelium. According to the growth pattern, it is classified as tubular, papillary, or tubulopapillary. Adenomas arising from the extrahepatic bile ducts usually produce symptoms related to biliary obstruction.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|gastrointestinal disease

name: malignant biphasic mesothelioma
description: A malignant neoplasm arising from mesothelial cells in the pleura. It is characterized by the presence of neoplastic epithelioid cells and sarcomatoid features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: bladder flat intraepithelial lesion
description: A non-papillary neoplasm of the urinary bladder, whose classification categories include low-grade intraurothelial neoplasia and urothelial carcinoma in situ.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: bladder inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
description: A multinodular intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the bladder. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: blast phase chronic myelogenous leukemia, BCR-ABL1 positive
description: An advanced phase of chronic myelogenous leukemia. It is characterized by: 1. the presence of blasts in the peripheral blood or bone marrow that are at least 20% of the peripheral blood white cells or of the nucleated cells in the bone marrow respectively, or 2. an extramedullary proliferation of blasts, and/or 3. when there are large aggregates and clusters of blasts in the bone marrow biopsy specimen (adapted from WHO, 2001).
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: breast carcinoma by gene expression profile
description: A header term that includes the following breast carcinoma subtypes determined by gene expression profiling: luminal A breast carcinoma, luminal B breast carcinoma, HER2 positive breast carcinoma, basal-like breast carcinoma, triple-negative breast carcinoma, and normal breast-like subtype of breast carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: breast diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the breast. It is the most common type of primary breast lymphoma.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: breast fibrosis
description: Breast fibrocystic change characterized by the prominence of fibrotic changes in the parenchyma.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: breast mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
description: An extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of mucosa associated lymphoid tissue that arises from the breast as a primary tumor.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: C-cell hyperplasia
description: Neoplastic or reactive proliferation of the C-cells in the thyroid gland. The neoplastic C-cell hyperplasia is associated with familial medullary thyroid gland carcinoma and multiple endocrine neoplasia type II and IIB. Morphologically, it is characterized by the presence of clusters of intrafollicular C-cells with atypical cytologic features. The reactive C-cell hyperplasia is also known as physiological or secondary C-cell hyperplasia and it is associated with conditions that cause hypercalcemia (e.g., hyperparathyroidism).
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder

name: calcifying fibrous tumor
description: A benign well-circumscribed paucicellular lesion arising from the soft tissues. It is characterized by the presence of fibroblasts, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, collagenous stroma formation, psammoma bodies, and dystrophic calcifications.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: calcifying nested epithelial stromal tumor of the liver
description: A rare malignant tumor that arises from the liver and occurs in children. It is characterized by the presence of nested epithelioid and spindle cells. Desmoplasia, calcifications, and bone formation may also be present.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|hepatobiliary disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: cardiac rhabdomyoma
description: A well circumscribed benign tumor arising from cardiac muscle. It usually affects children and may be present in the fetus. Depending on tumor location and size, cardiac, respiratory, and hemodynamic parameters may be affected. There is an association between cardiac rhabdomyoma and tuberous sclerosis.
therapeutic_areas: cardiovascular disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: cecum neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the cecum. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: central nervous system anaplastic large cell lymphoma
description: An anaplastic large cell lymphoma that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|infectious disease|nervous system disorder|hematologic disorder

name: central nervous system neoplasm
description: A benign or malignant, primary or metastatic neoplasm that affects the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. Representative examples of primary neoplasms include astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma, and meningioma. Representative examples of metastatic neoplasms include carcinoma and leukemia.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: cerebellar liponeurocytoma
description: A rare, WHO grade II cerebellar neoplasm which shows consistent neuronal, variable astrocytic and focal lipomatous differentiation. It occurs in adults, has a low proliferative potential and usually has a favorable prognosis. (Adapted from WHO)
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: cervical adenoid basal carcinoma
description: A rare low grade carcinoma that arises from the cervix. It is characterized by the presence of nests of basaloid cells with focal glandular formations.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: A rare carcinoma that arises from the cervix. It is characterized by the presence of cystic spaces surrounded by palisaded epithelial cells. The cystic spaces contain eosinophilic hyaline material or mucin. Nuclear pleomorphism, necrotic changes, and a high mitotic rate are also present.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical adenosquamous carcinoma
description: An uncommon carcinoma arising from the cervix. It is composed of malignant glandular epithelial cells and malignant squamous epithelial cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical clear cell adenocarcinoma
description: A rare morphologic variant of cervical adenocarcinoma composed of clear and hobnail cells. It is associated with in utero exposure to diethylstilbestrol (DES).
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2/3
description: A neoplastic process in the cervix characterized by morphologic features of both moderate and severe intraepithelial neoplasia.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
description: A rare, aggressive neuroendocrine carcinoma that arises from the cervix and is characterized by the presence of malignant cells with abundant cytoplasm, large nuclei, and prominent nucleoli.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical metaplasia
description: Metaplastic changes in the cervical glandular or squamous epithelium.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma, minimal deviation variant
description: A rare, extremely well differentiated cervical mucinous adenocarcinoma in which most of the neoplastic glands cannot be distinguished from the normal endocervical glands.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical villoglandular adenocarcinoma
description: A cervical adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of a prominent villoglandular pattern.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical small cell carcinoma
description: A small cell carcinoma arising from the cervix.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma arising from the cervical epithelium. It usually evolves from a precancerous cervical lesion. Increased numbers of sexual partners and human papillomavirus (HPV) infection are risk factors for cervical squamous cell carcinoma. The following histologic patterns have been described: conventional squamous cell carcinoma, papillary squamous cell carcinoma, transitional cell carcinoma, lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma, verrucous carcinoma, condylomatous carcinoma and spindle cell carcinoma. Survival is most closely related to the stage of disease at the time of diagnosis.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: cervical Wilms tumor
description: An embryonal neoplasm arising from the cervix with morphologic features resembling Wilms tumor of the kidney.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: chondroid chordoma
description: A slow-growing malignant bone tumor arising from the remnants of the notochord and occurring in the base of the skull. The tumor is characterized by a lobulated growth pattern, myxoid stroma formation, and the presence of physaliphorous cells and cartilage.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: chondroid hamartoma
description: A hamartoma that is characterized by the presence of chondroid elements.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: clear cell papillary cystadenoma
description: A benign cystic glandular epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic clear or hobnail cells which form papillary structures. There is no evidence of stromal invasion.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: colon Burkitt lymphoma
description: A rare Burkitt lymphoma that arises from the colon.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|infectious disease|gastrointestinal disease|genetic, familial or congenital disease|cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder

name: colon dysplasia
description: A morphologic finding indicating the presence of dysplastic glandular epithelial cells in the colonic mucosa. There is no evidence of invasion.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease

name: colon inflammatory polyp
description: A non-neoplastic polypoid lesion in the colon. It may arise in a background of inflammatory bowel disease or colitis. It is characterized by the presence of a distorted epithelium, inflammation, and fibrosis.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: colon juvenile polyp
description: A non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon. It is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|phenotype

name: colon mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
description: An extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue that arises from the colon.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: colon neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the colon. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: colon sessile serrated adenoma/polyp
description: A polyp that arises from the colon. It is characterized by the presence of serrated glands and the absence of generalized dysplasia. Some authors have suggested that it is a precursor lesion for some colonic adenocarcinomas with microsatellite instability.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: colorectal adenosquamous carcinoma
description: An unusual colorectal carcinoma characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous carcinomatous components. The two carcinomatous components may be admixed within the tumor, or the two may appear separately in different areas.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: colorectal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the colon or rectum.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|hematologic disorder

name: colorectal gastrointestinal stromal tumor
description: A gastrointestinal stromal tumor that arises from the colon or rectum. The majority of cases have spindle cell morphology. Gastrointestinal stromal tumors of the colon are usually advanced upon detection and tend to have a poor prognosis; gastrointestinal stromal tumors of the rectum usually have an aggressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: colorectal hamartoma
description: A non-neoplastic, hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon and rectum. This group includes the juvenile polyp, Peutz-Jeghers polyp, and Cowden-associated polyp.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|phenotype

name: colorectal juvenile polyp
description: A non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the colon and rectum. It is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|phenotype

name: colorectal neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the colon or rectum. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: colorectal serrated adenocarcinoma
description: A rare, invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of a malignant infiltrate with serrated glandular architecture.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: colorectal sessile serrated adenoma/polyp
description: A polyp that arises from the colon or rectum. It is characterized by the presence of serrated glands and the absence of generalized dysplasia. Some authors have suggested that it is a precursor lesion for some colorectal adenocarcinomas with microsatellite instability.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: colorectal squamous cell carcinoma
description: A very rare colorectal carcinoma characterized by the presence of a malignant squamous cell infiltrate.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: columnar cell hyperplasia of the breast
description: A columnar cell lesion characterized by the presence of enlarged terminal ductal lobular units with dilated acini. The acini are lined by more than two layers of columnar epithelial cells. Prominent apical cytoplasmic snouts are present. Secretions are often present in the lumina of the dilated acini.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: combined lung carcinoma
description: A lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of large or small neuroendocrine carcinoma cells in combination with malignant glandular or squamous epithelial cells.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: complex endometrial hyperplasia
description: A hyperplasia characterized by excessive proliferation of endometrial cells, resulting in the formation of complex epithelial structures. Epithelial atypia may be present or absent.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: conjunctival disorder
description: Any disorder of the conjunctiva.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system

name: conjunctival nevus
description: A benign melanocytic neoplasm that arises from the conjunctiva.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|disorder of visual system|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: conjunctival squamous cell carcinoma
description: A low-grade squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the conjunctiva. It is the most common primary malignant tumor that arises from the conjunctiva. It usually affects older white males. Excessive exposure to sunlight is a risk factor. Patients may present with a mass, red eye, or pain.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: cortisol-producing adrenal cortex adenoma
description: An adenoma of the adrenal cortex that produces cortisol. It may be associated with Cushing syndrome. Clinical presentation includes weight gain, round face, easy bruising, muscle weakness, emotional changes, hirsutism, and hypertension.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: cribriform carcinoma
description: A carcinoma characterized by the presence of a cribriform architectural pattern. Representative examples include the intraductal cribriform breast carcinoma and invasive cribriform breast carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: dedifferentiated solitary fibrous tumor
description: A solitary fibrous tumor characterized by the presence of areas of abrupt transition to high grade sarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: desmoplastic ameloblastoma
description: An ameloblastoma with prominent desmoplastic stroma that causes compression of the neoplastic epithelial islands.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: digestive system adenoma
description: A sporadic or less frequently familial neoplasm, arising from the glandular epithelium of the stomach, small intestine, biliary tract, colon, and rectum. It is a polypoid or flat circumscribed lesion. Morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. According to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. The dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The frequency of malignant transformation depends on the size of the lesion and the degree of dysplasia. Larger adenomas with severe dysplastic changes (sometimes called carcinoma in situ) carry a higher risk of progressing to invasive adenocarcinoma. Gastrointestinal adenomas may present as solitary or multifocal lesions. Familial adenomas tend to be multifocal and carry a higher risk of malignant transformation.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: digestive system carcinoma
description: A malignant neoplasm that arises from the epithelium of any part of the digestive system. Representative examples include colorectal carcinoma, esophageal carcinoma, and pancreatic carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: digestive system mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the digestive system and is characterized by the presence of a malignant glandular epithelial component and a malignant neuroendocrine component. At least 30% of either component should be present for the diagnosis to be made.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis
description: A rare, benign process that affects the peritoneal cavity and is characterized by the formation of multiple small nodules that are composed of well differentiated smooth muscle. It usually affects adults in their late reproductive years. Most patients are asymptomatic. The tumor nodules may regress spontaneously.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: ductal breast carcinoma in situ and lobular carcinoma in situ
description: The co-existence of ductal and lobular carcinoma in situ in the breast, without evidence of stromal invasion.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: duodenal adenocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the duodenum.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: duodenal villous adenoma
description: A neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the duodenum. It is characterized by a villous architectural pattern. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of childhood
description: An Epstein-Barr virus-associated mature T-cell lymphoproliferative group of disorders affecting children. It occurs with increased frequency in Asians and Native Americans. It includes the systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma of childhood and the hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoma.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: eccrine porocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma with eccrine differentiation arising from the sweat glands. It may arise de novo or as a malignant transformation of a pre-existing poroma. It usually grows in the legs, buttocks, feet, and trunk and usually presents as an ulcerative plaque. It is characterized by the presence of intraepidermal and dermal nests of malignant epithelial cells. It may recur after excision and metastasize to the lymph nodes and less frequently to distal anatomic sites.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: endolymphatic sac tumor
description: An aggressive epithelial neoplasm arising from the temporal bone. It is characterized by the presence of a papillary pattern, and has been described as an adenoma or carcinoma in the literature. There is disagreement regarding its relationship to endolymphatic sac tumor.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of ear|cancer or benign tumor

name: endometrial clear cell adenocarcinoma
description: A clear cell adenocarcinoma that involves the endometrium.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma
description: A primary endometrial adenocarcinoma composed of neoplastic cells that form complex glandular patterns associated with budding and branching of the neoplastic glands. The neoplastic glands resemble those of the normal endometrium and may or may not be associated with sheet-like proliferation of malignant cells. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most commonly seen morphologic variant of endometrial adenocarcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: endometrial hyperplasia without atypia
description: Simple or complex endometrial hyperplasia characterized by the absence of epithelial atypia.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: endometrial polyp
description: A benign nodular lesion protruding above the surface of the endometrium. It is composed of a fibrous stroma that contains thick-walled blood vessels and dilated endometrial glands. Polypectomy is the treatment of choice. Only few cases with recurrence have been reported.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: endometrial serous adenocarcinoma
description: A high grade, aggressive adenocarcinoma arising from the endometrium. It is characterized by the presence of complex papillary patterns with cellular budding. Atypical mitoses, necrosis, and psammoma bodies may be present. It is classified as type II endometrial carcinoma and it is not associated with endometrial hyperplasia. It tends to invade deeply into the myometrium and spreads into the lymphatic vessels. Patients frequently present with spread of the tumor beyond the uterus at the time of diagnosis. The prognosis is usually poor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: endometrial small cell carcinoma
description: A primary carcinoma of the endometrium that is similar to the small cell carcinoma of the lung, histologically.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: endometrial squamous cell carcinoma
description: A primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant squamous cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: endometrial undifferentiated carcinoma
description: A primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant cells that lack evidence of differentiation.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: epithelioid cell uveal melanoma
description: A uveal melanoma characterized by the presence of malignant large epithelioid melanocytes.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|cancer or benign tumor|disorder of visual system|nervous system disorder

name: ethmoid sinus adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that affects the ethmoid sinus.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: extrahepatic bile duct adenosquamous carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. It is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous malignant epithelial components.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: extrahepatic bile duct squamous cell carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the extrahepatic bile ducts. It is composed entirely by malignant squamous epithelial cells.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: fallopian tube carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the fallopian tube.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: fallopian tube carcinosarcoma
description: A carcinosarcoma that arises from the fallopian tube. It usually affects postmenopausal women and presents with abdominal pain, abdominal distension or genital bleeding. The prognosis is usually poor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: fallopian tube serous adenocarcinoma
description: A serous adenocarcinoma that arises from the fallopian tube. It is usually a high grade invasive adenocarcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: fibroblastic neoplasm
description: A benign, intermediate, or malignant mesenchymal neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic fibroblasts.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma
description: A distinctive type of liver cell carcinoma that arises in non-cirrhotic livers and is seen predominantly in young patients. The tumor cells are polygonal and deeply eosinophilic, and are embedded in a fibrous stroma. The prognosis is similar to classical hepatocellular carcinoma that arises in non-cirrhotic livers, and better than hepatocellular carcinoma that arises in cirrhotic livers.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|hepatobiliary disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: fibrous hamartoma of infancy
description: A poorly circumscribed neoplasm arising from the soft tissues in infants. It is characterized by the presence of bland fibroblastic spindle cells, collagenous stroma formation, primitive mesenchymal round cells, and mature fat cells. These components combined form a distinct organoid pattern.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: flat urothelial hyperplasia
description: A type of hyperplasia that is characterized by a marked thickening of the urinary tract epithelium. There is no evidence of cytologic atypia. -- 2003
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: floor of mouth mucoepidermoid carcinoma
description: A mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the oral cavity that arises from the floor of the mouth.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: follicular variant thyroid gland papillary carcinoma
description: A nonencapsulated variant of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid gland characterized by the predominance of follicular structures. The malignant follicular cells display the nuclear features that characterize the papillary adenocarcinomas of the thyroid gland.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: gallbladder adenocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from glandular epithelial cells of the gall bladder.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gallbladder adenoma
description: A polypoid epithelial neoplasm that arises from the gallbladder. According to the neoplastic growth pattern, it is classified as tubular, tubulopapillary, or papillary.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: gallbladder adenosquamous carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the gallbladder. It is characterized by the presence of glandular and squamous malignant epithelial components.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gallbladder biliary intraepithelial neoplasia
description: A neoplastic, non-invasive lesion that affects the gallbladder epithelium. It is characterized by the presence of atypical epithelial cells with an increased nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio, nuclear hyperchromasia, and loss of nuclear polarity.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gallbladder small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
description: An aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the gallbladder. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|hepatobiliary disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: gallbladder squamous cell carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the gallbladder. It is composed entirely by malignant squamous epithelial cells.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric adenoma
description: A neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach. This category includes intestinal-type adenomatous polyps, gastric-type adenomas, and fundic gland polyps.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: gastric choriocarcinoma
description: A malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the stomach. It is characterized by the presence of syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast cellular components. It is often associated with lymph node and hematogenous metastases.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: gastric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: An extranodal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the stomach with the bulk of the mass located in the stomach.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric hamartomatous polyp
description: A non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of connective tissue stroma overgrowth and cystic formations.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: gastric mantle cell lymphoma
description: A mantle cell lymphoma that affects the stomach. It may arise as a solitary mass or it may be a component of multifocal lymphomatous polyposis of the gastrointestinal tract. It usually has an aggressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder|gastrointestinal disease

name: gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
description: A low grade, indolent B-cell lymphoma, usually associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. Morphologically it is characterized by a dense mucosal atypical lymphocytic (centrocyte-like cell) infiltrate with often prominent lymphoepithelial lesions and plasmacytic differentiation. Approximately 40% of gastric MALT lymphomas carry the t(11;18)(q21;q21). Such cases are resistant to Helicobacter pylori therapy.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the stomach. The vast majority of cases arise from the corpus-fundus region. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent. It may be associated with autoimmune chronic atrophic gastritis, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1, or it may be sporadic.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric papillary adenocarcinoma
description: A variant of gastric adenocarcinoma with exophytic growth and elongated finger-like processes lined by cylindrical or cuboidal cells supported by fibrovascular connective tissue cores.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
description: An aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the stomach. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastric squamous cell carcinoma
description: A rare carcinoma of the stomach resembling squamous cell carcinomas arising elsewhere in the body.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: gastrointestinal hamartoma
description: A non-neoplastic, hamartomatous polyp that arises from the stomach, small intestine, and large intestine. This group includes the juvenile polyps and Peutz-Jeghers polyps.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: giant cell tumor of soft tissue
description: A painless, well circumscribed tumor arising in soft tissue, usually of the upper and lower extremities. Morphologically, it is characterized by a multinodular growth pattern. The cellular infiltrate is composed of mononuclear round or oval cells and multinucleated osteoclast-like giant cells, in a rich vascular stroma. It rarely metastasizes.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: gonadal teratoma
description: A teratoma that arises from the testis or ovary.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: grade III prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia
description: High grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of severe architectural and cytologic abnormalities.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: granular cell tumor
description: An unusual benign or malignant neoplasm characterized by the presence of neoplastic large polygonal cells with granular, eosinophilic cytoplasm which contains abundant lysosomes. It was originally thought to be a tumor originating from muscle cells and was named granular cell myoblastoma. Subsequent studies have suggested a derivation from Schwann cells. It affects females more often than males and it usually presents as a solitary mass. A minority of patients have multiple tumors. It can arise from many anatomic sites including the posterior pituitary gland, skin, oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, heart, mediastinum, and breast.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: granulocytic sarcoma
description: A tumor mass composed of myeloblasts, neutrophils and neutrophil precursors. Granulocytic sarcoma is the most common type of myeloid sarcoma. (WHO, 2001)
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: growth hormone-producing pituitary gland adenoma
description: An adenoma of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that produces growth hormone. The vast majority of cases are hormonally functioning and are associated with either gigantism or acromegaly.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: head and neck paraganglioma
description: A benign or malignant extra-adrenal paraganglioma arising from paraganglia in the head and neck. Representative examples include the carotid body and jugulotympanic paragangliomas.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: hepatic granuloma
description: A granuloma located in the liver.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|endocrine system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: hepatoid adenocarcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma with morphologic characteristics similar to hepatocellular carcinoma, arising from an anatomic site other than the liver.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: HER2 positive breast carcinoma
description: A biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by high expression of HER2, GRB7, and TRAP100, and by lack of expression of estrogen receptor (ER).
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: hidradenocarcinoma
description: A carcinoma with apocrine and less often eccrine differentiation, arising from the sweat glands. It usually presents as a solitary slow growing nodule in the dermis or subcutaneous tissues. It is characterized by a nodular growth pattern and it is often associated with necrotic changes.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: high grade surface osteosarcoma
description: A usually aggressive high grade malignant bone-forming mesenchymal neoplasm arising from the surface of the bone.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: histiocytic and dendritic cell neoplasm
description: Rare tumors that affect the hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues. The cells of origin are the histiocytes and accessory cells. They can occur at any age and show no significant variations in geographical distribution. This category includes the histiocytic sarcoma, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, Langerhans cell sarcoma, interdigitading dendritic cell sarcoma/tumor, follicular dendritic cell sarcoma/tumor, and dendritic cell sarcoma, not otherwise specified. (WHO, 2001)
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: hydatidiform mole
description: A gestational trophoblastic disorder characterized by marked enlargement of the chorionic villi, hyperplasia of the villous trophoblastic cells and hydropic changes.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|cancer or benign tumor|pregnancy or perinatal disease|reproductive system or breast disease

name: hyperplastic polyp
description: A polyp found mainly in the stomach and colon. Microscopically, it is characterized by elongated, serrated crypts lined by proliferative epithelium. Hyperplastic polyps are traditionally considered non-neoplastic, but ras mutation is common, clonality has been demonstrated and biochemical abnormalities and epidemiological associations that occur in colorectal adenomas and carcinomas have been found (WHO Tumors of the Digestive System, 2000).
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: ileal neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the ileum. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: intestinal type adenocarcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma arising from epithelium which has undergone intestinal metaplasia. Representative examples include gastric, gallbladder, and ampulla of Vater intestinal type adenocarcinomas.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: intimal sarcoma
description: A malignant neoplasm arising from the large blood vessels. It is characterized by the presence of tumor cells that grow within the lumen of the blood vessels. The intraluminal tumor growth may result in vascular obstruction and spread of tumor emboli to peripheral organs. The prognosis is usually poor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: invasive breast carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that infiltrates the breast parenchyma. The vast majority are adenocarcinomas arising from the terminal ductal lobular unit (TDLU). Often, the invasive adenocarcinoma co-exists with ductal or lobular carcinoma in situ. It is the most common carcinoma affecting women.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: jejunal neuroendocrine tumor G1
description: A well differentiated, low grade neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid tumor) that arises from the jejunum. The mitotic count is less than 2 per 10 HPF and/or the Ki67 index is equal to or less than 2 percent.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: juvenile polyp
description: A non-neoplastic hamartomatous polyp that arises from the stomach and intestinal tract. It is characterized by the presence of tortuous and cystically dilated glands, edematous changes, and inflammation.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: kidney medullary carcinoma
description: A type of renal carcinoma affecting mostly young African-Americans. It is located in the medulla of the kidney, and follows an aggressive clinical course. Most reported cases have shown metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: A adenoid cystic carcinoma that involves the lacrimal gland.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: laryngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: A rare adenoid cystic carcinoma of the larynx. It usually arises from the supraglottic or subglottic area. It is characterized by slow progression and late distant metastases.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: laryngeal small cell carcinoma
description: A rare carcinoma that arises from the larynx. It is characterized by the presence of small neuroendocrine cells. It metastasizes early and has an aggressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease

name: Leydig cell tumor
description: A sex cord-stromal tumor occurring in the testis and rarely in the ovary. It is predominantly or completely composed of Leydig cells which may contain crystals of Reinke. In males it usually presents as a painless testicular enlargement and it may be associated with gynecomastia and decreased libido. The majority of the cases have a benign clinical course. Approximately 10% of the cases have a malignant clinical course and metastasize. In females it may be associated with androgenic manifestations and it follows a benign clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: liver cavernous hemangioma
description: A hemangioma with cavernous vascular spaces arising from the liver. It is the most frequent benign tumor of the liver and usually affects young females.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|cardiovascular disorder|endocrine system disorder|hepatobiliary disorder|cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: liver diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A rare diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the liver and the bulk of the tumor is located in the liver.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder|gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|hepatobiliary disorder

name: lobular breast carcinoma in situ
description: A non-invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast characterized by a proliferation of monomorphic cells completely filling the lumina. The overall lobular architecture is preserved. It is frequently multifocal (90% in some series) and bilateral. It seldom becomes invasive; however there is an increased risk of infiltrating ductal adenocarcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: low grade central osteosarcoma
description: A low grade osteosarcoma arising from the medullary portion of the bone. It affects the long bones and is characterized by the presence of fibroblastic stroma and osteoid production. Pain and swelling are the usual sign and symptom. The prognosis is more favorable than conventional osteosarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma
description: A low grade, late-metastasizing variant of fibrosarcoma characterized by alternating fibrous and myxoid areas and a whorling growth pattern. The neoplastic cells have a spindle morphology, and lack hyperchromasia or significant nuclear atypia. Approximately 40% of cases show the focal presence of collagen rosettes. A t(7;16)(q33;p11) translocation has been identified in the majority of cases, associated with the presence of FUS-CREB3L2 fusion protein. Rare cases carry the t(11;16)(p11;p11) translocation which is associated with the presence of the FUS-CREB3L1 fusion protein.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma with giant collagen rosettes
description: A low grade fibromyxoid sarcoma characterized by the presence of prominent collagen rosettes.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: low grade vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
description: An intraepithelial lesion of the vulvar squamous epithelium that represents the clinical and morphological manifestation of a productive HPV infection. Low grade refers to the associated low risk of concurrent or future cancer. (WHO, 2014)
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: lung giant cell carcinoma
description: A morphologic variant of lung sarcomatoid carcinoma characterized by the presence of mononuclear and multinucleated pleomorphic neoplastic giant cells that lack cohesion.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype

name: lung inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
description: An intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the lung. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: lung lymphangioleiomyomatosis
description: Lymphangiomyomatosis involving the lungs and local lymph nodes. Patients usually present with chylous pleural effusion. The clinical course is variable. Patients with resectable lesions usually have a favorable clinical outcome. Patients with diffuse lesions usually have a progressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: lung papilloma
description: A benign papillary neoplasm that arises endobronchially. It is classified as squamous cell, glandular, or mixed squamous cell and glandular papilloma. Patients usually present with signs and symptoms of bronchial obstruction.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: lung sarcomatoid carcinoma
description: A rare, aggressive, poorly differentiated, non-small cell lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of a sarcomatoid component often associated with giant cell differentiation. There is a male to female ratio of 4:1. Clinical symptoms include cough, hemoptysis, chest pain, progressive dyspnea and fever secondary to recurrent pneumonia. Cigarette smoking is a major risk factor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype

name: lung sclerosing hemangioma
description: A benign tumor that arises from the lung. It is characterized by the presence of sclerotic, papillary, solid, and hemorrhagic patterns and hyperplastic type II pneumocytes. Cholesterol clefts, hemosiderin deposition, chronic inflammation, and calcifications may be present. In the majority of cases, it is a solitary and peripheral tumor. Patients are usually asymptomatic.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cardiovascular disorder|phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: lung signet ring cell carcinoma
description: A morphologic variant of lung adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of signet ring cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype

name: lymphangiosarcoma
description: A malignant neoplasm arising from the endothelial cells of the lymphatic vessels.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: lymphoepithelioma-like lung carcinoma
description: A morphologic variant of large cell lung carcinoma characterized by the presence of a syncytial growth pattern, large vesicular nuclei with esophnophilic nucleoi, and dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: major salivary gland carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the parotid gland, submandibular gland, or sublingual gland.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: major salivary gland carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from a pleomorphic adenoma in the major salivary glands. It usually originates in the parotid gland. Patients usually present with a history of a long-standing tumor mass which grew rapidly in the past few months. Patients with non-invasive or minimally invasive carcinoma have an excellent prognosis. In cases where there is invasion of the surrounding tissues, the clinical course is aggressive.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: major salivary gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the major salivary glands. It usually arises from the parotid gland. It is the most common primary carcinoma of the salivary glands and usually presents as a firm and painless mass. It is characterized by the presence of epidermoid cells, mucus producing cells, and cells of intermediate type. The majority of cases have a favorable outcome.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: malignancy in giant cell tumor of bone
description: A malignant tumor that arises from the bone. It is characterized by the presence of an area of high grade sarcoma in an otherwise typical giant cell tumor (primary malignancy in giant cell tumor), or the presence of sarcoma in which the pre-existing giant cell tumor may or may not be apparent (secondary malignancy in giant cell tumor).
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: malignant adrenal gland pheochromocytoma
description: A pheochromocytoma that metastasizes to other anatomic sites. Common sites of metastasis include lymph nodes, bones, liver, and lung. Morphologic features associated with malignant pheochromocytomas include: atypical mitotic figures, capsular and vascular invasion, tumor cell necrosis, and high mitotic activity.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: malignant germ cell tumor
description: A gonadal or extragonadal malignant neoplasm that arises from germ cells. Representative examples include embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, and seminoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: malignant jugulotympanic paraganglioma
description: A jugulotympanic paraganglioma that metastasizes to other anatomic sites.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|endocrine system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: malignant mesothelioma
description: A malignant neoplasm of the pleura or peritoneum, arising from mesothelial cells. It is associated with exposure to asbestos.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: pleural cancer
description: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm affecting the pleura. A representative example of primary malignant pleural neoplasm is the malignant pleural mesothelioma. A representative example of metastatic malignant neoplasm to the pleura is metastatic carcinoma that has spread to the pleura from another anatomic site.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: malignant urinary system neoplasm
description: A primary or metastatic malignant tumor involving the urinary system. Common tumor types include carcinomas, lymphomas, and sarcomas.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: maxillary sinus adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the maxillary sinus. It usually has an aggressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|respiratory or thoracic disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: mediastinal malignant germ cell tumor
description: An extragonadal malignant germ cell tumor that arises from the mediastinum. This category includes seminoma, embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, mixed germ cell tumors, and immature malignant teratoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: medullomyoblastoma with myogenic differentiation
description: A rare malignant embryonal neoplasm arising from the cerebellum. It is characterized by the morphologic features of a medulloblastoma and the presence of a striated muscle component. Its clinical behavior is similar to medulloblastoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: metanephric adenoma
description: A benign, well-circumscribed renal cortical neoplasm affecting females more often than males. Polycythemia has been reported in twelve-percent of patients.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: micropapillary serous carcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of complex micropapillary structures covered by round and cuboidal cells with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: middle ear squamous cell carcinoma
description: A rare squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the middle ear.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of ear|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: minor salivary gland adenocarcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma that arises from the minor salivary glands.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: mixed lobular and ductal breast carcinoma
description: A breast carcinoma characterized by the presence of a lobular and a ductal component. The ductal component comprises less than 50 percent of the tumor.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: mixed somatotroph-lactotroph pituitary gland adenoma
description: An infrequent pituitary gland adenoma composed of an admixture of acidophilic and chromophobic cells that produce growth hormone and prolactin respectively. Unlike mammosomatotroph adenomas, these two hormones are not localized in the same cell by immunohistochemistry.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: mucinous gastric adenocarcinoma
description: A variant of gastric adenocarcinoma with more than half of the tumor containing extracellular mucinous pools.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm
description: A category of clonal hematopoietic disorders that have both myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features at the time of initial presentation.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor|genetic, familial or congenital disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: myofibroma
description: A benign, localized, nodular and well-circumscribed neoplasm usually seen as a congenital neoplasm or in the first year of life. It is characterized by a biphasic growth pattern and is composed of small, undifferentiated mesenchymal cells associated with branching thin-walled vessels and more mature neoplastic spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm in a collagenous stroma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: nabothian cyst
description: A benign, mucus-filled cervical cyst that occurs when mucus-secreting columnar epithelial cells are covered with squamous epithelium.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: nasal cavity polyp
description: A soft and painless polypoid mass that arises from the mucosa in the nasal cavity. It is usually the result of an inflammatory process. It may recur following surgical resection.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|respiratory or thoracic disease

name: neuroblastic tumor
description: A group of nervous system tumors which display neuronal differentiation. It includes tumors that are composed of immature round cells and tumors that display advanced differentiation and the formation of ganglion cells.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: neurothekeoma
description: A benign neoplasm arising from nerve sheaths. It is characterized by the presence of a myxoid stroma.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: non-cutaneous melanoma
description: Melanoma is a malignant tumor of melanocytes, cells that are derived from the neural crest. Although most melanomas arise in the skin, they also may arise from mucosal surfaces or at other sites to which neural crest cells migrate. (PDQ)
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: non-functioning adrenal cortex adenoma
description: An adenoma of the adrenal cortex characterized by the absence of a hormonal syndrome or symptoms suggestive of adrenal disease.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: non-neoplastic bile duct disorder
description: A non-neoplastic disorder that affects the intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts. Representative examples include cholangitis and biliary atresia.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease

name: non-seminomatous lesion
