description: A group of testicular cancers that begin in the germ cells (cells that give rise to sperm). Nonseminomas are identified by the type of cell in which they begin and include embryonal carcinoma, teratoma, choriocarcinoma, and yolk sac carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: normal breast-like subtype of breast carcinoma
description: A biologic subset of breast carcinoma defined by high expression of many genes expressed by adipose and other non-epithelial tissues.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: ocular melanoma
description: A melanoma that arises from the structures of the eye or ocular adnexa.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: ocular melanoma with extraocular extension
description: A melanoma arising from and extending beyond the structures of the eye.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: ocular sebaceous carcinoma
description: Ocular sebaceous carcinoma is a rare condition and accounts for 1% to 5.5% of eyelid malignancies and is the third most common eyelid malignancy after basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma. It usually affects elderly women, has a high rate of local recurrence, and a tendency to regional and distant metastases.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system|integumentary system disorder|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: odontogenic cyst
description: A cyst in the jaw that arises from tissues of tooth development.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: olfactory neuroblastoma
description: An olfactory neuroblastoma arising in the paranasal sinus.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: ossifying fibromyxoid tumor
description: A rare soft tissue tumor of uncertain lineage characterized by the presence of neoplastic spindle to round cells forming cords in a fibromyxoid stroma. The lesions are associated with the formation of metaplastic bone. Most patients present with painless subcutaneous masses. Recurrences have been reported in a minority of patients.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: ovarian endometrioid adenocarcinoma
description: An endometrioid adenocarcinoma arising from the ovary. It comprises 10% to 25% of all primary ovarian carcinomas. Grossly, endometrioid carcinoma may present as a cystic or solid mass. Microscopically, the tumor greatly resembles the appearance of the ordinary type of endometrial adenocarcinoma. As a group, endometrioid carcinoma has a prognosis twice as good as that of serous or mucinous carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder

name: ovarian endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation
description: An endometrioid adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary and exhibits squamous differentiation. The squamous cell component often has a cytologically benign appearance.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder

name: ovarian endometriosis
description: A non-neoplastic disorder characterized by the growth of endometrial tissue in the ovaries. It results in the development of blood filled ovarian cysts (chocolate cysts), and creation of scars and adhesions.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: ovarian microcystic stromal tumor
description: A benign, unilateral tumor that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of conspicuous microcystic changes, cellular areas, and a fibrous stroma.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: ovarian serous adenofibroma
description: A benign neoplasm of the ovary characterized by the presence of glands with serous epithelial cells in a fibrotic stroma.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: ovarian transitional cell carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from the ovary and is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells that resemble malignant urothelial cells. There is no morphologic evidence of a benign or borderline Brenner tumor component present.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: ovarian yolk sac tumor
description: A usually rapidly growing malignant germ cell tumor arising from the ovary. It usually occurs in children and adolescents. Signs and symptoms include abdominal pain and a large abdominal or pelvic mass. The serum alpha-fetoprotein is almost always elevated preoperatively. Morphologically, there is marked heterogeneity due to numerous patterns of differentiation coexisting in the same tumor. The most common pattern is reticular.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma arising from the pancreas. It is characterized by the presence of relatively uniform malignant cells which form acinar patterns. It usually occurs during adulthood. Signs and symptoms include abdominal pain, weight loss, nausea, and diarrhea. It may metastasize to regional lymph nodes and the liver. A minority of patients develop lipase hypersecretion syndrome. This syndrome may be seen in patients with liver metastases and it is characterized by excessive secretion of lipase in the serum, polyarthralgia, and subcutaneous fat necrosis.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|phenotype

name: pancreatic large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
description: An aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the pancreas. It is characterized by the presence of malignant large cells.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: pancreatic small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
description: An aggressive, high-grade and poorly differentiated carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the pancreas. It is characterized by the presence of malignant small cells.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: papillary cystic neoplasm
description: A benign, malignant, or borderline neoplasm characterized by the presence of papillary mucinous, serous, or clear cell structures and cystic structures.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: papillary transitional cell carcinoma
description: A non-invasive or invasive transitional cell carcinoma characterized by a papillary growth pattern. It may occur in the bladder or the renal pelvis.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: parachordoma
description: A rare, usually benign myoepithelial tumor characterized by the presence of epithelioid, often vacuolated neoplastic cells. Most patients present with painless swelling in the subcutaneous or subfascial soft tissues of the extremities.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: paranasal sinus adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: A rare adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the paranasal sinuses. It usually has an aggressive clinical course characterized by high recurrence rates and distant metastases.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: paranasal sinus Schneiderian papilloma
description: A papilloma that arises from the ciliated respiratory mucosa that lines the paranasal sinuses. It is classified as inverted papilloma and oncocytic papilloma.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: parathyroid hyperplasia
description: A hyperplasia that involves the parathyroid gland.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: parotid gland acinic cell carcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma with serous acinar cell differentiation that arises from the parotid gland. Patients usually present with a slow growing mass in the parotid area.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: parotid gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An aggressive carcinoma that arises from the parotid gland. It is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial and myoepithelial cells forming cribriform, tubular, and solid patterns. It usually presents as a slow growing mass. Patients develop pain because of the tendency of these carcinomas to invade perineural tissues.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: parotid gland carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from a pleomorphic adenoma in the parotid gland. Patients usually present with a history of a long-standing tumor mass which grew rapidly in the past few months. Patients with non-invasive or minimally invasive carcinoma have an excellent prognosis. In cases where there is invasion of the surrounding tissues, the clinical course is aggressive.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: parotid gland squamous cell carcinoma
description: An invasive squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the parotid gland. It usually affects elderly patients and presents as a rapidly enlarging tumor mass, often associated with pain.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: neoplasm with perivascular epithelioid cell differentiation
description: A soft tissue neoplasm composed of perivascular epithelioid cells. Representative examples include angiomyolipoma, clear cell-sugar-tumor of the lung, and lymphangioleiomyomatosis.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: penile carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the penis
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: peritoneal mesothelioma
description: A benign or malignant mesothelial neoplasm that arises from the peritoneum.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: peritoneal multicystic mesothelioma
description: A cystic mesothelioma that arises from the peritoneum and usually affects young to middle aged females. Grossly, it presents as a large multiloculated tumor mass, usually in the pelvic peritoneum. Histologically it is characterized by the presence of multiple cysts that are lined by one or more layers of mesothelial cells that do not show atypia. Patients usually present with abdominal or pelvic mass and pain. The clinical course is indolent. The tumor may recur, but transformation to diffuse malignant mesothelioma is rare.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: peritoneal well differentiated papillary mesothelioma
description: A localized or multifocal mesothelioma arising from the peritoneum. It predominantly occurs in women. It is characterized by the formation of papillae, covered by a single layer of blunt mesothelial cells. Mitotic figures are not present. There is no evidence of severe cytologic atypia. It has a relatively favorable clinical outcome, compared to diffuse malignant mesothelioma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: Peutz-Jeghers polyp
description: A hamartomatous polyp that occurs in the stomach, small and large intestines, and rarely within the esophagus, nasopharynx and the urinary tract. The Peutz-Jeghers polyps are grossly lobulated and dark. Microscopically, they have a central core of smooth muscle covered by mucosa. The smooth muscle shows tree-like branching. The question of whether or not the Peutz-Jeghers polyp is precancerous is a matter of controversy. The loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 19p (where the responsible gene LKB1 is located) suggests that the increased risk of malignancy may be due to malignant transformation from hamartoma to adenocarcinoma. --2002
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: Peutz-Jeghers polyp of the stomach
description: A non-neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach and is characterized by the presence of smooth muscle branching bands, and hyperplasia with cystic dilatation of the foveolar epithelium.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: pharyngeal adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the pharynx.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor
description: An extremely rare, benign or malignant mesenchymal tumor arising from the soft tissues or bones. It is a distinctive tumor, which usually displays the following morphologic characteristics: low cellularity, myxoid changes, presence of spindled cells and osteoclasts, hemangiopericytoma-like vessels, hemorrhage, and osteoid-like matrix. It is associated with the presence of a paraneoplastic syndrome called osteogenic osteomalacia. This syndrome usually precedes the appearance of the tumor, and it is characterized by phosphaturia, hypophosphatemia, normal serum calcium levels, and decreased levels of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3. Patients present with bone and muscle pain, severe muscle weakness, fractures, gait disturbances, skeletal deformity, height loss, and slow growth. The metabolic disturbances improve or completely disappear after the complete resection of the tumor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation
description: A WHO grade II or III pineal parenchymal neoplasm of intermediate-grade malignancy, affecting all ages. It is composed of diffuse sheets or large lobules of uniform cells with mild to moderate nuclear atypia and low to moderate level mitotic activity. (Adapted from WHO)
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: pituicytoma
description: An extremely rare, WHO grade I, circumscribed and slow-growing tumor that arises from the neurohypophysis or infundibulum and described in adults. It is characterized by the presence of elongated, spindle-shaped neoplastic glial cells that form storiform patterns or interlacing fascicular arrangements. Signs and symptoms include visual disturbances, headache, amenorrhea, and decreased libido.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|nervous system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: pituitary gland adenoma
description: A non-metastasizing tumor that arises from the adenohypophysial cells of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland. The tumor can be hormonally functioning or not. The diagnosis can be based on imaging studies and/or radioimmunoassays. Due to its location in the sella turcica, expansion of the tumor mass can impinge on the optic chiasm or involve the temporal lobe, third ventricle and posterior fossa A frequently associated physical finding is bitemporal hemianopsia which may progress to further visual loss.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: placental choriocarcinoma
description: Choriocarcinoma that develops in the placenta. It is the rarest form of gestational choriocarcinoma. Metastases to the mother and infant may occur.
therapeutic_areas: pregnancy or perinatal disease|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: placental hemangioma
description: A hemangioma arising from the fetal blood vessels in the placental villi.
therapeutic_areas: cardiovascular disorder|pregnancy or perinatal disease|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: pleural biphasic mesothelioma
description: Malignant mesothelioma that arises from the pleura. It is characterized by the presence of epithelioid and sarcomatoid components, with each component representing at least 10% of the tumor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: pleural epithelioid mesothelioma
description: Malignant mesothelioma that arises from the pleura and is characterized by the presence of cells with epithelioid morphology. The epithelioid cells usually have eosinophilic cytoplasm, bland nuclei, and form tubulopapillary, microglandular, or sheet-like patterns.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: pleural sarcomatoid mesothelioma
description: Malignant mesothelioma that arises from the pleura and is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped cells forming fascicles, or that are distributed haphazardly resembling a sarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: plexiform ameloblastoma
description: A histologic variant of solid/multicystic ameloblastoma characterized by the presence of basal cells forming anastomosing strands and cords in a delicate stroma.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: poorly differentiated thyroid gland carcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma arising from the thyroid gland showing only limited evidence of follicular cell differentiation. Microscopically, the adenocarcinoma cells are arranged in insular, solid, and trabecular patterns. There is associated necrosis, and vascular invasion. The prognosis depends on the tumor stage, complete or partial surgical removal of the tumor, and the degree of response to radioactive iodine therapy (adapted from WHO Tumors of Endocrine Organs, IARC Press, Lyon 2004)
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, Leg type
description: An aggressive primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma, usually involving the lower leg. It is composed of a generally monotonous proliferation of immunoblasts, or less frequently centroblasts, with few admixed reactive cells. This type of lymphoma occurs most often in elderly women who present with rapidly growing tumors, usually on one or both legs. Dissemination to extracutaneous sites is frequent. Treatment with combination chemotherapy is usually required.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: primary intraosseous squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises centrally from the jaw. It derives from odontogenic epithelial remnants. It includes solid type squamous cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma that arises from an odontogenic cyst, and squamous cell carcinoma that derives from a keratocystic odontogenic tumor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: primary peritoneal serous adenocarcinoma
description: A rare, serous adenocarcinoma that diffusely involves the pelvic peritoneum seen predominantly in elderly postmenopausal women. Exclusion of serous carcinoma arising from the ovary and fimbrial end of fallopian tube is required to diagnose the above entity.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: primary pulmonary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that is localized to the lungs at the time of presentation. Signs and symptoms include cough, dyspnea, and hemoptysis.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder|respiratory or thoracic disease|phenotype

name: prolactin-producing pituitary gland carcinoma
description: A rare, hormonally functioning or non-functioning pituitary gland adenocarcinoma that produces prolactin.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: prostate rhabdomyosarcoma
description: A malignant mesenchymal neoplasm with skeletal muscle differentiation affecting the prostate.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: prostate small cell carcinoma
description: A neuroendocrine carcinoma of the prostate gland with unfavorable prognosis, composed of small cells containing neurosecretory granules. Approximately half of the cases show a mixture of small cells and adenocarcinoma cells.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: pyloric gland adenoma
description: A rare neoplastic polyp that arises from the stomach. It is characterized by the presence of gastric epithelial differentiation and pyloric gland-type tubular structures, which are closely packed.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: rectal hyperplastic polyp
description: A serrated polypoid lesion that arises in the rectum. It rarely produces symptoms. This group includes goblet cell rich, mucin poor, and microvesicular hyperplastic polyps.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: rectal traditional serrated adenoma
description: An adenoma that arises from the rectum. It is characterized by prominent serration of the glands and the presence of generalized low-grade dysplasia.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: rectal tubular adenoma
description: A usually polypoid neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the rectal mucosa. It is characterized by a tubular architectural pattern. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: rectal tubulovillous adenoma
description: A neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the rectal mucosa. It is characterized by tubular and villous architectural patterns. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: rectal villous adenoma
description: A neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the rectal mucosa. It is characterized by a villous architectural pattern. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: renal cell carcinoma associated with Xp11.2 translocations/TFE3 gene fusions
description: A group of kidney carcinomas characterized by the presence of different translocations involving the chromosome Xp11.2. These translocations result in the creation of gene fusions involving the TFE3 gene. Patients are usually children and young adults. Morphologically, the malignant epithelial cells form papillary patterns.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: retroperitoneal inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
description: A multinodular intermediate fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the retroperitoneum. It is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, and a chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed of eosinophils, lymphocytes and plasma cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: salivary gland acinic cell carcinoma
description: A carcinoma of the salivary gland characterized by serous acinar cell differentiation. The vast majority of cases occur in the parotid gland. It usually presents as a slowly enlarging mass. A minority of patients experience pain. It may recur or metastasize. Multiple recurrences and metastasis to cervical lymph nodes are usually associated with a poor prognosis.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: salivary gland adenosquamous carcinoma
description: A rare, aggressive carcinoma that arises from the salivary glands. It is characterized by the presence of a squamous and a glandular epithelial component.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: salivary gland basal cell adenocarcinoma
description: A rare adenocarcinoma of the major and minor salivary glands, originating from basaloid, myoepithelial and ductal cells. While morphologically resembling basal cell carcinomas, it is a distinct entity. The tumor is not encapsulated, may invade locally, and less frequently may metastasize. It usually occurs in older patients.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: salivary gland carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from a pleomorphic adenoma in the salivary glands. It usually originates in the parotid gland. Patients usually present with a history of a long-standing tumor mass which grew rapidly in the past few months. Patients with non-invasive or minimally invasive carcinoma have an excellent prognosis. In cases where there is invasion of the surrounding tissues, the clinical course is aggressive.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: salivary gland large cell carcinoma
description: A rare, highly aggressive carcinoma that arises from the salivary gland, predominantly the parotid gland. It is characterized by the presence of large pleomorphic malignant cells with abundant cytoplasm. Patients usually present with a rapidly growing mass.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: salivary gland small cell carcinoma
description: An infrequent small cell carcinoma that arises from the salivary glands and is characterized by the presence of a high number of mitotic figures.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: sarcomatoid carcinoma
description: A malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of spindle cells and anaplastic morphologic features. Giant cells and a sarcomatous component may also be present.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: sarcomatoid mesothelioma
description: A diffuse malignant mesothelioma arising from the pleura and less often the peritoneum. It is characterized by the presence of spindle cells. Anaplastic morphologic features and multinucleated malignant cells may also be seen.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: sex hormone-producing adrenal cortex adenoma
description: A rare adenoma of the adrenal cortex that produces androgens or estrogens.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: signet ring cell gastric adenocarcinoma
description: A poorly cohesive gastric adenocarcinoma characterized by malignant cells containing intracytoplasmic mucin.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: simple endometrial hyperplasia
description: A proliferation of endometrial cells resulting in glandular enlargement and budding without changes in the basic structure of the endometrium. Epithelial atypia may be present or absent.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
description: A rare, highly aggressive carcinoma that arises from the sinonasal tract. It is characterized by the presence of small to medium size malignant cells. The prognosis is poor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy
description: A rare disorder of unknown etiology characterized by distention of the lymph node sinuses and sinusoidal histiocytic infiltration. The histiocytes characteristically contain ingested lymphocytes. Patients present with cervical lymphadenopathy, fever, leukocytosis, and hypergammaglobulinemia. It can affect extranodal sites, including skin, bones, and the respiratory tract. It usually regresses spontaneously.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder

name: skin sarcoma
description: A sarcoma that arises from the skin. Representative examples include Kaposi sarcoma, angiosarcoma, lymphangiosarcoma, liposarcoma, and leiomyosarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: small intestinal Burkitt lymphoma
description: A Burkitt lymphoma that arises from the small intestine.
therapeutic_areas: infectious disease|immune system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: small intestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that arises from the small intestine.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|hematologic disorder|gastrointestinal disease

name: small intestinal enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
description: An enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma arising from the small intestine, most commonly the jejunum or ileum. Patients usually present with abdominal pain, often associated with intestinal perforation. There is often a history of celiac disease. The lymphoma cells are usually medium-sized to large and form an ulcerating mucosal lesion with invasion of the small intestinal wall. Villous atrophy is present in the adjacent small intestinal mucosa. In a minority of cases the lymphoma cells are medium-sized and form a monomorphic infiltrate.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: small intestinal intraepithelial neoplasia
description: A precancerous neoplastic process that affects the small intestine. It is characterized by low or high grade dysplasia of the mucosal epithelium. There is no evidence of invasion.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: small intestinal mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
description: A mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma (MALT) that arises from the small intestine. The morphologic characteristics are similar to those seen in gastric MALT lymphomas, with the exception of the lymphoepithelial lesions that are less prominent in the small intestine.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: small intestinal tubular adenoma
description: A usually polypoid neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the small intestine. It is characterized by a tubular architectural pattern. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: small intestinal tubulovillous adenoma
description: A neoplasm that arises from the glandular epithelium of the small intestine. It is characterized by tubular and villous architectural patterns. The neoplastic glandular cells have dysplastic features.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: soft tissue chondroma
description: A benign neoplasm arising from the extraskeletal soft tissues near tendons and joints. It is a well circumscribed tumor characterized by the presence of chondrocytes, a lobulated hyaline cartilage growth pattern, and in some cases calcification.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: soft tissue neoplasm
description: A benign, intermediate, or malignant neoplasm that arises from the soft tissue. The most common types are lipomatous (fatty), vascular, smooth muscle, fibrous, and fibrohistiocytic neoplasms.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: spinal cord primitive neuroectodermal tumor
description: A central nervous system embryonal tumor, not otherwise specified arising from the spinal cord.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: spindle cell melanoma
description: A melanoma characterized by the presence of malignant spindle-shaped melanocytes.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: splenic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma occurring in the spleen.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: splenic hodgkin lymphoma
description: A rare Hodgkin lymphoma that arises from the spleen.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|infectious disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: splenic mantle cell lymphoma
description: A mantle cell lymphoma occurring in the spleen.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: stromal predominant kidney Wilms tumor
description: Wilms tumor of the kidney characterized by the predominance of the mesenchymal component.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: submandibular gland adenocarcinoma
description: An adenocarcinoma that arises from the submandibular gland. Representative examples include polymorphic low-grade adenocarcinoma and acinic cell carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: submandibular gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An aggressive carcinoma that arises from the submandibular gland. It is characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial and myoepithelial cells forming cribriform, tubular, and solid patterns. It usually presents as a slow growing mass. Patients develop pain because of the tendency of these carcinomas to invade perineural tissues.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: synovial chondromatosis
description: Synovial chondromatosis is a type of non-cancerous tumor that arises in the lining of a joint. The knee is most commonly affected, however it can affect any joint. The tumors begin as small nodules of cartilage. These nodules can separate and become loose within the joint. Some tumors may be no larger than a grain of rice. Synovial chondromatosis most commonly occurs in adults ages 20 to 50. Signs and symptoms may include pain, swelling, a decreased range of motion, and locking of the joint. The exact underlying cause of the condition is unknown. Treatment may involve surgery to remove the tumor. Recurrence of the condition is common.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: tendon sheath fibroma
description: A small, slow growing, benign neoplasm arising from the tendon sheaths. The tumor is characterized by the presence of spindle-shaped fibroblasts and collagenous stroma formation.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: teratoma with malignant transformation
description: A teratoma which is characterized by morphologic transformation to malignancy and an aggressive clinical course. The malignant component most often is sarcomatous or carcinomatous.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: testicular embryonal carcinoma
description: A malignant germ cell neoplasm arising from the testis. It is composed of primitive epithelial cells arranged in solid, papillary, and glandular configurations. Most patients present with a testicular mass, which may be associated with pain. More than half of the patients have metastatic disease at diagnosis. The form of treatment following radical orchiectomy is stage dependent.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
description: A testicular germ cell tumor characterized by the absence of a seminomatous component. It includes embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, teratoma, and mixed forms.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: therapy-related myeloid neoplasm
description: Acute myeloid leukemias, myelodysplastic syndromes, and myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms arising as a result of the mutagenic effect of chemotherapy agents and/or radiation that are used for the treatment of neoplastic or non-neoplastic disorders.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor|genetic, familial or congenital disease|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: thymic carcinoma
description: Thymic carcinoma (TC) is a type of thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by a high malignant potential.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thymic sarcomatoid carcinoma
description: A rare, usually aggressive, primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by the presence of tumor cells morphologically resembling soft tissue sarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thymic undifferentiated carcinoma
description: A rare primary thymic carcinoma, characterized by an undifferentiated solid tumor growth, without associated sarcomatoid features.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thymoma
description: A neoplasm arising from the epithelial cells of the thymus. Although thymomas are usually encapsulated tumors, they may invade the capsule and infiltrate the surrounding tissues or even metastasize to distant anatomic sites. The following morphologic subtypes are currently recognized: type A, type B, type AB, metaplastic, micronodular, microscopic, and sclerosing thymoma. Thymomas type B are further subdivided into types B1, B2, and B3. Thymoma type B3 usually has the most aggressive clinical course.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thymoma type B3
description: Also known as well-differentiated thymic carcinoma, atypical thymoma, or epithelial thymoma, this type of thymoma displays morphologic characteristics of a well-differentiated carcinoma. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage II or stage III tumors. It is almost always invasive, it recurs frequently, and metastasizes in approximately 20% of the cases.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thymoma type B1
description: A thymic epithelial neoplasm characterized by the presence of expanded areas which resemble the normal thymic cortex. The neoplastic epithelial cells are small and scant and there is a dense T-lymphocytic component present. Areas of medullary differentiation with or without Hassall's corpuscles are also present. It may be associated with myasthenia gravis, pure red cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia. It has a low grade malignant potential. The majority of cases occur in the anterior mediastinum as Masaoka stage I tumors. A minority of the cases occur as stage II tumors.
therapeutic_areas: hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroglossal duct cyst
description: A congenital benign cyst arising from the remnants of the thyroglossal duct. It is usually located in the midline of the neck.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroid gland diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
description: A diffuse large B-cell lymphoma primarily involving the thyroid gland.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|hematologic disorder

name: thyroid gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma
description: A primary, low grade carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of groups of squamoid and mucous cells, surrounded by fibrous tissue. Prominent cystic structures may be present. The clinical course is usually indolent.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroid gland mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma
description: An extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma arising from mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue in the thyroid gland. The vast majority of cases are associated with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|immune system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroid gland spindle cell tumor with thymus-like differentiation
description: A rare, slow growing, primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland characterized by a lobulated architectural pattern and the presence of a biphasic cellular population composed of spindle epithelial cells and glandular cells. A small number of cases are composed exclusively of spindle epithelial cells or glandular cells.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroid gland squamous cell carcinoma
description: A rapidly growing primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of malignant squamous cells. The clinical course is usually aggressive.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: thyroid gland undifferentiated (anaplastic) carcinoma
description: A primary carcinoma of the thyroid gland composed of undifferentiated cells. The malignant cells demonstrate evidence of epithelial differentiation, either by immunohistochemistry or electron microscopic studies. Microscopically, in the majority of cases there is a mixture of spindle, epithelioid, and giant cells. The vast majority of the patients present with a rapidly enlarging neck mass. The clinical course is usually aggressive.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: tibial adamantinoma
description: An adamantinoma arising from the tibia. The tibia is the site which is more frequently involved by adamantinoma (80-90% of cases).
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: tonsillar squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma that arises from the mucosal lining of the tonsil and tends to metastasize early to the lymph nodes. It predominantly affects middle aged and elderly patients who have a history of alcohol and tobacco use. Patients may present with tonsillar swelling, sore throat, pain radiating to the ipsilateral ear, or a neck mass.
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|respiratory or thoracic disease|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: tracheal adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the trachea. It spreads to the submucosal tracheal tissue and to regional lymph nodes.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: transitional cell carcinoma
description: A malignant neoplasm arising from the transitional epithelium, usually affecting the urinary bladder, ureter, or renal pelvis. It may or may not have a papillary configuration. It is graded 1 to 3 or 4 according to the degree of cellular differentiation and architectural patterns. Grade 1 transitional cell carcinoma is histologically benign but it may recur. Transitional cell carcinomas may also affect the upper respiratory tract and the ovaries.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: undifferentiated gallbladder carcinoma
description: A carcinoma without evidence of differentiation arising from the gallbladder. The most common variant is the spindle and giant cell type which resembles a sarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: undifferentiated ovarian carcinoma
description: An aggressive carcinoma arising from the ovary. Most patients present with advanced disease. Microscopically, it is characterized by significant cytologic atypia, increased mitotic activity, and necrosis. The prognosis is usually poor.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|endocrine system disorder|reproductive system or breast disease

name: undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma
description: A carcinoma with poor prognosis that arises from the pancreas. It is characterized by the presence of a significant malignant component that does not show differentiation. The malignant cells represent a mixture of large, pleomorphic cells and giant cells, or adenocarcinoma cells and spindle cells, or spindle cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|phenotype

name: undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells
description: A rare variant of undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma characterized by the presence of non-neoplastic osteoclast-like giant cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease|endocrine system disorder|phenotype

name: undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma, inflammatory variant
description: An undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma characterized by the presence of numerous inflammatory cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: ureter carcinoma
description: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the ureter.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: ureter small cell carcinoma
description: A rare carcinoma that arises from the ureter. It is characterized by the presence of small neuroendocrine cells. The prognosis is poor.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor|phenotype

name: urothelial dysplasia
description: A morphologic finding indicating the presence of dysplastic changes in the transitional cell epithelium of the urinary tract.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: usual ductal breast hyperplasia
description: A neoplastic ductal proliferative lesion of the breast characterized by the formation of secondary lumens and prominent intraductal proliferation of a heterogeneous cellular population that may include epithelial cells, myoepithelial cells, or metaplastic apocrine cells.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: uterine carcinosarcoma
description: A usually aggressive malignant neoplasm arising from the uterine corpus and less often the cervix. It is characterized by the presence of two components: a malignant epithelial component and a sarcomatous component. In the uterine corpus the epithelial component is usually glandular whereas in the cervix is usually non-glandular. Carcinosarcoma of the cervix, although it is aggressive, it may have a better prognosis compared to the uterine corpus carcinosarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: uveal melanoma
description: A melanoma derived from melanocytes of the uveal tract. It is the most common primary intraocular tumor in the United States and Western Europe. Similar to melanoma of the skin, it is rare in Africa and Asia. Diagnostic procedures include ophthalmoscopic exam, fluorescein angiography and ultrasound. Treatment includes: surgical excision of the eye, iridocyclectomy and tumor resection. Recent treatments also include radiotherapy or photo coagulation. Classification of uveal melanomas recognizes four cell types within these tumors: epithelioid, intermediate, mixed cell, and spindle cell types. The spindle cell type uveal melanomas are further sub-classified as spindle cell type A and spindle cell type B.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|disorder of visual system|cancer or benign tumor|nervous system disorder

name: vaginal adenoid cystic carcinoma
description: An adenoid cystic carcinoma that arises from the vagina. Myoepithelial cells are usually not present.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: vaginal carcinosarcoma
description: An aggressive mixed epithelial and mesenchymal neoplasm that arises from the vagina and is characterized by the presence of a malignant epithelial component and a malignant mesenchymal component.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: vaginal melanoma
description: A primary malignant neoplasm of the vagina composed of malignant melanocytes.
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: vaginal squamous cell carcinoma
description: A squamous cell carcinoma arising from the vagina. Human papillomavirus infection is associated with the development of vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia and invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Signs and symptoms include painless bleeding, postcoital bleeding, and urinary tract symptoms. Morphologically it resembles squamous cell carcinomas in other anatomic sites. Radiation therapy is the preferred treatment for most cases. The prognosis is related to the stage of the disease.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|reproductive system or breast disease

name: vulvar lichen sclerosus
description: A chronic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology that affects the vulva. It is characterized by the development of white elevated plaques in the vulva. Histologically there is marked subepithelial fibrosis. Clinical manifestations include pruritus, dysuria, and dyspareunia.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|reproductive system or breast disease|phenotype

name: Warthin tumor
description: An adenoma characterized by an oncocytic, often papillary, epithelial component, dense lymphoid stroma, and cystic spaces. It occurs primarily in the parotid gland, and is the second most common benign parotid salivary gland tumor. A strong association with smoking has been reported. It typically presents as a painless swelling in the lower portion of the parotid gland.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: palsy
description: A general term most often used to describe severe or complete loss of muscle strength due to motor system disease from the level of the cerebral cortex to the muscle fiber. This term may also occasionally refer to a loss of sensory function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p45)
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder

name: cerebral palsy
description: A group of disorders affecting the development of movement and posture, often accompanied by disturbances of sensation, perception, cognition, and behavior. It results from damage to the fetal or infant brain.
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder

name: adenomatous colon polyp
description: A polypoid adenoma that arises from and protrudes into the lumen of the colon. Epithelial dysplasia is always present. According to the architectural pattern it is classified as tubular, tubulovillous, or villous.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: hamartoma
description: A benign and excessive tumor-like growth of mature cells and normal tissues which grow in a disorganized pattern.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|cancer or benign tumor

name: hemangioma
description: A benign vascular lesion characterized by the formation of capillary-sized or cavernous vascular channels.
therapeutic_areas: cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: acute respiratory distress syndrome
description: Progressive and life-threatening pulmonary distress in the absence of an underlying pulmonary condition, usually following major trauma or surgery. Cases of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome are not included in this definition.
therapeutic_areas: respiratory or thoracic disease

name: acquired metabolic disease
description: An instance of metabolic disease that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.
therapeutic_areas: nutritional or metabolic disease

name: basal ganglia cerebrovascular disorder
description: A pathological condition caused by impaired blood flow in the basal regions of cerebral hemispheres (basal ganglia), such as infarction; hemorrhage; or ischemia in vessels of this brain region including the lateral lenticulostriate arteries. Primary clinical manifestations include involuntary movements (dyskinesias) and muscle weakness (hemiparesis).
therapeutic_areas: nervous system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|phenotype

name: congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia
description: Any one of a group of congenital hemolytic anemias in which there is no abnormal hemoglobin or spherocytosis and in which there is a defect of glycolysis in the erythrocyte. Common causes include deficiencies in glucose-6-phosphate isomerase; pyruvate kinase; and glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|hematologic disorder|phenotype

name: hereditary hemochromatosis
description: An inherited metabolic disorder characterized by iron accumulation in the tissues.
therapeutic_areas: genetic, familial or congenital disease|nutritional or metabolic disease

name: papillary carcinoma
description: A malignant epithelial neoplasm characterized by a papillary growth pattern. A papillary carcinoma may be composed of glandular cells (papillary adenocarcinoma), squamous cells (papillary squamous cell carcinoma), or transitional cells (papillary transitional cell carcinoma). Bladder carcinoma is a representative example of papillary transitional cell carcinoma.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: renal tubular transport disease
description: Genetic defects in the selective or non-selective transport functions of the kidney tubules.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder

name: estrogen-receptor positive breast cancer
description: A subtype of breast cancer that is estrogen-receptor positive
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: estrogen-receptor negative breast cancer
description: A subtype of breast cancer that is estrogen-receptor negative
therapeutic_areas: reproductive system or breast disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: acute pancreatitis
description: An acute inflammatory process that leads to necrosis of the pancreatic parenchyma. Signs and symptoms include severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, and shock. Causes include alcohol consumption, presence of gallstones, trauma, and drugs.
therapeutic_areas: endocrine system disorder|gastrointestinal disease|phenotype

name: childhood malignant neoplasm
description: A malignant tumor that occurs in children. Representative examples include soft tissue and bone sarcomas (e.g. osteosarcoma) and embryonal neoplasms (e.g. hepatoblastoma and rhabdoid tumor).
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor

name: rectal cancer
description: A primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm that affects the rectum. Representative examples include carcinoma, lymphoma, and sarcoma.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: Achenbach syndrome
description: A rare disorder which affects the volar surfaces of fingers. Clinical signs include recurrent, spontaneous or post-traumatic bruising of fingers. The clinical course of the resultant hematoma usually follows a pattern of resolution within days.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: acneiform dermatitis
description: Cutaneous eruptions resembling acne, characterized by the presence of papulonodules, pustules, comedones, or cysts in the face, trunk, and extremities. Causes include infections and the use of certain medications (e.g., antibiotics and steroids).
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: acquired keratosis
description: Focal or diffuse thickening of the skin not inherited as a primary genetic disorder. Causes include inflammatory skin disorders, infectious disorders, lymphedema, and medications.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: acrodermatitis
description: An inflammatory skin condition affecting children. It is often associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection, hepatitis B infection or cytomegalovirus infection. It is characterized by the presence of cutaneous rashes and patches on the palms and soles. The trunk is not affected.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans
description: An acrodermatitis characterized by a chronically progressive course, leading to widespread atrophy of the skin. It is a clinical manifestation of Lyme borreliosis.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: allergic contact dermatitis
description: An inflammatory skin condition caused by an immune response to direct contact between the skin and an allergen. It consists of a delayed type of allergic reaction at the affected site with resulting red, swollen, and blistered skin that may itch or leak.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|phenotype

name: allergic urticaria
description: A urticaria with a basis in a pathological type I hypersensitivity reaction.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|phenotype

name: anhidrosis
description: Lack of sweating or the ability to sweat when provoked by the appropriate stimulus.
therapeutic_areas: phenotype|integumentary system disorder

name: bacterial exanthem
description: A bacteria-induced exanthem
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|infectious disease|phenotype

name: cholesteatoma
description: A pathologic process characterized by the proliferation of keratinizing squamous epithelium resulting in the accumulation of keratin and cells in the middle ear and/or mastoid. It may be congenital or acquired. If left untreated, it may increase in size and destroy adjacent structures.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: cholesteatoma of attic
description: A cholesteatoma in the attic
therapeutic_areas: disorder of ear|integumentary system disorder

name: cholesteatoma of external ear
description: A cholesteatoma (disease) that involves the external ear.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of ear|integumentary system disorder

name: cholesteatoma of middle ear
description: A non-neoplastic lesion characterized by the proliferation of keratinizing squamous epithelium in the middle ear that results in the accumulation of keratin and cells. It is usually caused by repeated infections. If left untreated, it may increase in size and destroy the adjacent delicate bones of the middle ear.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of ear|integumentary system disorder

name: cholinergic urticaria
description: A type of physical urticarias (or hives) that appears when a person is sweating.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: congenital generalized lipodystrophy
description: An extremely rare autosomal recessive condition, characterized by an extreme scarcity of fat in the subcutaneous tissues.
therapeutic_areas: nutritional or metabolic disease|integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|phenotype

name: conjunctival pigmentation
description: Pigmented lesions that arise from the conjunctiva include nevus, complexion-associated melanosis (CAM), primary acquired melanosis (PAM), and malignant melanoma.1,2All of these lesions arise from melanocytes. However, a number of other lesions have a similar appearance but a different source, such as pigment deposits from silver and iron.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system

name: diffuse lipomatosis
description: A neoplastic process characterized by a diffuse poorly circumscribed overgrowth of adipose tissue. It has been associated with several genetic disorders and different clinical conditions such as liver disease, excessive alcohol intake, adrenocortical steroid therapy, and antiretroviral therapy.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: dyshidrosis
description: A recurrent eczematous reaction characterized by the development of vesicular eruptions on the palms and soles, particularly along the sides and between the digits. It is accompanied by pruritus, a burning sensation, and hyperhidrosis. The disease is self-limiting, lasting only a few weeks. (Dorland, 27th ed)
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: epidermolysis bullosa
description: Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) is a group of genetic skin diseases that cause the skin to blister very easily. Blisters form in response to minor injuries or friction, such as rubbing or scratching. There are four main types of epidermolysis bullosa: dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa Epidermolysis bullosa simplex Junctional epidermolysis bullosa Kindler Syndrome Identifying the exact type can be hard because there are many subtypes of EB. Within each type or subtype, a person may be mildly or severely affected. The disease can range from being a minor inconvenience to completely disabling, and fatal in some cases. Most types of EB are inherited. The inheritance pattern may be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive. Management involves protecting the skin, reducing friction against the skin, and keeping the skin cool.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: epidermolysis bullosa dystrophica
description: A genetic skin disorder caused by mutations in the type VII collagen gene (COL7A1). It is characterized by the formation of blisters and scarring in the skin and mucous membranes.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: erythema infectiosum
description: A self-limited viral infectious disorder caused by the human parvovirus B19. It affects predominantly children and is characterized by the development of a bright red skin eruption in the cheeks. It is followed by a maculopapular skin eruption in the extremities which eventually fades into a lacey pattern.
therapeutic_areas: infectious disease|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: erythema multiforme
description: Erythema multiforme (EM) refers to a group ofhypersensitivity disorders characterized by symmetric red, patchy lesions, primarily on the arms and legs. The cause is unknown, but EM frequently occurs in association with herpes simplex virus, suggesting an immunologic process initiated by the virus. In half of the cases, the triggering agents appear to be medications, including anticonvulsants, sulfonamides, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and other antibiotics. In addition, some cases appear to be associated with infectious organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae and many viral agents. Erythema multiforme is the mildest of three skin disorders that are often discussed in relation to each other. It is generally the mildest of the three. More severe is Stevens-Johnson syndrome. The most severe of the three is toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN).
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: erythematosquamous dermatosis
description: A skin condition that primarily affects the scalp and face and presents as scaly inflammation. Examples include itchy, dry skin and dandruff.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: exanthem
description: A skin disease characterized by widespread, often symmetrical skin eruption that typically occurs acutely in association with a systemic disease, especially infectious or immune-mediated conditions.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: facial dermatosis
description: Facial Dermatosis, also known as facial dermatoses, is related tolipogranulomatosis. An important gene associated with Facial Dermatosis isCCNE1(cyclin E1). The drugsbetamethasoneandbetamethasone acetatehave been mentioned in the context of this disorder.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: fibroepithelial polyp of the anus
description: A non-neoplastic polypoid lesion that arises from the anal canal or perianal skin. It is composed of dense fibrous stroma and it is covered by squamous epithelium.
therapeutic_areas: cancer or benign tumor|gastrointestinal disease

name: fibroepithelial polyp of urethra
description: A benign polypoid lesion of mesodermal origin that arises from the urethra.
therapeutic_areas: urinary system disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: alopecia mucinosa
description: A rare dermatologic disorder characterized by the accumulation of mucinous material in the hair follicles. In some cases it is associated with lymphoproliferative disorders, most often mycosis fungoides and Hodgkin lymphoma.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: folliculitis
description: Inflammation of the hair follicles. Causes include excessive perspiration, skin infections, and skin wounds.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: Fox-Fordyce disease
description: A chronic skin disease most common in women aged 13-35 years.It is characterized by the development of intense itching in the underarm area, the pubic area, and around the nipple of the breast as a result of perspiration which becomes trapped in the sweat gland and surrounding areas. The cause is unknown, but heat, humidity, and stress may play a role. Treatment may include the use of retinoids, antibiotics, and immunosuppressants.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: granuloma annulare
description: Granuloma annulare is a long-term (chronic) skin disease consisting of a rash with reddish bumps arranged in a circle or ring. The most commonly affected areas are the forearms, hands and feet. The lesions associated with granuloma annulare usually resolve without treatment. Strong steroids (applied as a cream or injection) are sometimes used to clear the rash more quickly. Most symptoms will disappear within 2 years (even without treatment), but recurrence is common. The underlying cause of granuloma annulare is unknown.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: granulomatous dermatitis
description: An inflammatory reaction of the skin to various organic and inorganic antigens. It is characterized by tumor-like masses or nodules of granulomatous tissue comprised of activated histiocytes, epitheliod cells, and multinucleated giant cells.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: hand dermatosis
description: Skin conditions characterized by dense infiltration of inflammatory cells (neutrophils) in the affected tissue. They arise in reaction to some underlying systemic illness. A neutrophilic dermatosis may be seen in isolation or more than one type may occur in the same individual.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: hemangioma of subcutaneous tissue
description: A hemangioma arising from the subcutaneous soft tissues.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|cardiovascular disorder|cancer or benign tumor

name: pemphigoid gestationis
description: A rare pregnancy-associated autoimmune skin disease that is characterized by an itchy rash that develops into blisters. It is most common during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy. It was previously known as herpes gestationis although it has no association with the herpes virus whatsoever.
therapeutic_areas: pregnancy or perinatal disease|immune system disorder|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: hidradenitis suppurativa
description: A chronic suppurative and cicatricial disease of the apocrine glands occurring chiefly in the axillae in women and in the groin and anal regions in men. It is characterized by poral occlusion with secondary bacterial infection, evolving into abscesses which eventually rupture. As the disease becomes chronic, ulcers appear, sinus tracts enlarge, fistulas develop, and fibrosis and scarring become evident.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: eyelid hypopigmentation
description: Under-production of pigment in the eyelid.
therapeutic_areas: disorder of visual system

name: inverted follicular keratosis
description: Seborrheic keratosis that arises from follicular structures in the skin. It presents as a solitary nodule in the skin and is characterized by the presence of prominent squamous eddies.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: irritant dermatitis
description: An inflammatory skin condition caused by direct contact between the skin and an irritating substance. It is typically manifested by erythema, mild edema, and scaling at the affected site.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: juvenile dermatitis herpetiformis
description: Dermatitis herpetiformis in children
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: keratosis
description: A skin disorder consisting of hypertrophy of the stratum corneum of the skin.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: kernicterus due to isoimmunization
description: Encephalopathy in infants due to high levels of unconjugated bilirubin that are a result of Rh incompatibility between the mother and the fetus.
therapeutic_areas: pregnancy or perinatal disease|nervous system disorder|hematologic disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease|nutritional or metabolic disease|phenotype

name: leg dermatosis
description: A nonspecific term used to denote any cutaneous lesion or group of lesions, or eruptions of any type on the leg. (From Stedman, 25th ed)
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: lichen disease
description: A long-term skin condition that mainly affects the skin of the genitals. It usually causes itching and white patches to appear on the affected skin.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: lichen nitidus
description: A chronic inflammatory disease characterized by shiny, flat-topped, usually flesh-colored micropapules no larger than the head of a pin. Lesions are localized in the early stages, found chiefly on the lower abdomen, penis, and inner surface of the thighs. Distribution may become generalized as the disease progresses.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: lichen planus
description: A chronic, recurrent, pruritic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology that affects the skin and mucus membranes. It presents with rashes and papules that tend to resolve spontaneously. It may be associated with hepatitis C. Certain drugs that contain arsenic or bismuth are associated with reactions mimicking lichen planus.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: lipodystrophy
description: A congenital or acquired disorder characterized by abnormal loss or redistribution of the adipose tissue in the body.
therapeutic_areas: nutritional or metabolic disease|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: lipomatosis
description: A neoplastic process characterized by diffuse overgrowth of mature adipose tissue.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: Ludwig's angina
description: Severe cellulitis of the submaxillary space with secondary involvement of the sublingual and submental space. It usually results from infection in the lower molar area or from a penetrating injury to the mouth floor. (From Dorland, 27th ed)
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|integumentary system disorder|infectious disease|phenotype

name: maxillary sinus cholesteatoma
description: A rare, progressive, non-neoplastic pathologic process that arises from the maxillary sinus mucosal epithelium. It is characterized by the proliferation of keratinizing squamous epithelium and the formation of keratin sheets. It may lead to bone erosion and infections. Surgical removal is the appropriate treatment.
therapeutic_areas: gastrointestinal disease|respiratory or thoracic disease|integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: mediastinal lipomatosis
description: A neoplastic process characterized by a diffuse poorly circumscribed overgrowth of adipose tissue in the mediastinum.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: melanoacanthoma
description: A benign, darkly pigmented skin lesion characterized by proliferation of keratinocytes and melanocytes.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: miliaria
description: A small (one mm or less) vesicular, papular or pustular monomorphous rash, which is associated with heat, fever or occlusion of sweat glands.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: miliaria rubra
description: Miliaria rubraor prickly heat occurs deeper in the epidermis (outside layer of skin) and results in very itchy red papules (bumps).
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: mongolian spot
description: A benign, flat, congenital birthmark, with wavy borders and an irregular shape. The color is caused by melanocytes, melanin-containing cells, that are usually located in the surface of the skin (the epidermis), but are in the deeper region (the dermis) in the location of the spot.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: necrobiosis lipoidica
description: Necrobiosis lipoidica is a rare skin disorder of collagen degeneration. It is characterized by a rash that occurs on the lower legs. It is more common in women, and there are usually several spots. They are slightly raised shiny red-brown patches. The centers are often yellowish and may develop open sores that are slow to heal. Infections can occur but are uncommon. Some patients have itching, pain, or abnormal sensations. It usually occurs more often in people with diabetes, in people with a family history of diabetes or a tendency to get diabetes, but can occur in nondiabetic people. About 11% to 65% of patients with necrobiosis lipoidica also have diabetes, but the exact cause is still not known. Treatment is difficult. The disease is typically chronic with variable progression and scarring.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: neurodermatitis
description: Skin findings arising from repeated rubbing, picking or scratching of a real or imagined irritation of the skin.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: neurotic excoriation
description: A condition in which patients produce skin lesions through repetitive, compulsive excoriation of their skin.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: occupational dermatitis
description: Contact dermatitis associated with allergens or irritants found in the workplace.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: palmoplantar keratosis
description: A group of autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, X-linked inherited or acquired disorders characterized by the thickening of the palms and soles due to hyperkeratosis.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: panniculitis
description: Inflammation of the subcutaneous adipose tissue.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease

name: parapsoriasis
description: An inflammatory skin disorder of unknown etiology characterized by papules and plaques or scaly patches resembling psoriasis.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: pelvic lipomatosis
description: A neoplastic process characterized by a diffuse poorly circumscribed overgrowth of adipose tissue in the pelvic region. Clinical presentation includes complaints of back and abdominal pain, urinary frequency, perineal pain and constipation. It predominately affects black males.
therapeutic_areas: musculoskeletal or connective tissue disease|cancer or benign tumor

name: pemphigus
description: Pemphigus is a group of rare autoimmune diseases that cause blistering of the skin and mucous membranes (mouth, nose, throat, eyes, and genitals).This conditioncan occur at any age, but often strikes people in middle or older age. Studies have shown that some populations may be at greater risk for certain types of pemphigus. For instance, people of Jewish descent and those from India, Southeast Europe, and the Middle East are at greater risk for pemphigus vulargis, while pemphigus foliaceus is more common in North America, Turkey, and South America. Pemphigus is a chronic disease which is best controlled by early diagnosis and treatment.Treatment includes steroids to reduce inflammation,drugs that suppress the immune system responseand antibiotics to treat associated infections. There are four main types of pemphigus: Pemphigus vulgaris Pemphigus foliaceus IgA pemphigus Paraneoplastic pemphigus
therapeutic_areas: immune system disorder|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: perinatal jaundice due to hepatocellular damage
description: Jaundice in perinates due to cellular damage of liver.
therapeutic_areas: hepatobiliary disorder|endocrine system disorder|gastrointestinal disease

name: photoallergic dermatitis
description: A delayed hypersensitivity involving the reaction between sunlight or other radiant energy source and a chemical substance to which the individual has been previously exposed and sensitized. It manifests as a papulovesicular, eczematous, or exudative dermatitis occurring chiefly on the light-exposed areas of the skin.
therapeutic_areas: injury, poisoning or other complication|integumentary system disorder|immune system disorder|phenotype

name: photosensitivity disease
description: Abnormal responses to sunlight or artificial light due to extreme reactivity of light-absorbing molecules in tissues. It refers almost exclusively to skin photosensitivity, including sunburn, reactions due to repeated prolonged exposure in the absence of photosensitizing factors, and reactions requiring photosensitizing factors such as photosensitizing agents and certain diseases. With restricted reference to skin tissue, it does not include photosensitivity of the eye to light, as in photophobia or photosensitive epilepsy.
therapeutic_areas: injury, poisoning or other complication|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: phototoxic dermatitis
description: Dermatitis caused or precipitated by exposure to ultraviolet sunlight, or by mediating phototoxic or photoallergic material in response to ultraviolet sunlight.
therapeutic_areas: injury, poisoning or other complication|integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: physical urticaria
description: A distinct subgroup of the urticaria that are induced by an exogenous physical stimulus rather than occurring spontaneously.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: pityriasis rosea
description: A mild, self-limited skin disorder that is most commonly seen in children and young adults. It is characterized by an initial large round spot on the chest, abdomen, or back, often referred to as a herald patch, that is usually followed within a week by a distinctive pattern of similar but smaller papules on the torso, arms, and legs. There may also be itching, especially when overheated.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|phenotype

name: porokeratosis
description: A clonal proliferation of abnormal keratinocytes characterized by the development of localized or multiple atrophic skin patches surrounded by an annular keratotic ring called cornoid lamella.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder|genetic, familial or congenital disease

name: reactive cutaneous fibrous lesion
description: A benign, epidermal skin lesion characterized by overexpression of collagen during wound healing.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: rosacea
description: A chronic erythematous skin disorder that affects the face. It is characterized by the development of redness in the cheeks, nose, and/or forehead and telangiectasia. Sometimes, the erythematous changes may involve the eyelids.
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: scalp dermatosis
description: Dermotosis of scalp
therapeutic_areas: integumentary system disorder

name: scleredema adultorum
